core_findings: Google Services remains the dominant cash engine, combining Search/YouTube advertising with subscriptions/platforms/devices; Google Cloud is a second scaled engine; Other Bets remains economically small and loss-making.
Advertising was about 73.15% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, so diversification is meaningful but does not remove ad/search concentration.
Shared Alphabet-level AI R&D means segment margins do not represent fully loaded standalone economics.
unresolved_points: Exact product-level profit allocation within Services remains undisclosed.

core_findings: Services generated exceptional absolute operating profit while Cloud margin reached roughly 35% in Q2 2026.
The model combines digital distribution and auction economics with an increasingly capital-intensive AI infrastructure layer.
Network advertising is structurally weaker than Search/YouTube, preventing a single uniform quality label across all revenue.
unresolved_points: Fully loaded AI economics across Services and Cloud remain unallocated.

canonical_verdict_fields.PRIMARY_MOAT: Search/advertising scale, user habit, auction liquidity and distribution reinforced by data and product ecosystem
SUPPORTING_MECHANISMS: Cloud enterprise ecosystem and installed workloads

core_findings: Search usage share, browser/mobile distribution, advertiser demand, persistent query growth and extraordinary Services profit provide convergent behavioral and economic proof that the moat exists.
YouTube and Cloud add independent but less dominant reinforcing mechanisms.
The moat is not reducible to technical switching costs: default payments and distribution contracts matter, and remedies explicitly target them.
AI answer interfaces, publisher traffic pressure, interoperability mandates and strong rival models make moat trend UNCLEAR even while durability is judged LONG.
unresolved_points: AI-search monetization and publisher-equilibrium effects are not yet proven.

core_findings: Core runway is supported by Cloud/AI enterprise demand, Search AI monetization, YouTube/subscriptions and continued AI infrastructure deployment.
Cloud RPO and realized Cloud growth support capture evidence, but RPO is not treated as near-term revenue one-for-one.
Waymo and standalone Gemini consumer monetization remain optionality because unit economics / standalone revenues are not disclosed.
Runway requires exceptional reinvestment and is constrained by power, water, land, specialized suppliers, regulation and capital intensity.
unresolved_points: No defensible bottom-up total capture pool exists for consolidated Alphabet AI opportunity.

core_findings: FY2025 all-in operating ROIC is about 43%-44%; a financing bridge corroborates the denominator within roughly one percentage point.
R&D capitalization sensitivity still produces mid-30s ROIC, so strong returns are not an artifact of expensing all R&D.
The June 2026 capital base expands sharply because of AI infrastructure and acquisitions; a simple H1 annualized diagnostic falls into the high-30s.
ROIIC is NOT_INTERPRETABLE because current capital build, Wiz/Intersect and shared AI costs break clean period-to-period attribution.
unresolved_points: Incremental AI returns cannot yet be isolated.
Wiz/Intersect acquisition returns are not observable.

core_findings: Standardized FCF was roughly $73bn in both FY2024 and FY2025, then compressed to about $4.3bn in H1 2026 as capex almost matched CFO.
H1 2026 GAAP net income is not a cash-quality proxy because large investment fair-value gains dominate the earnings bridge.
SBC is material and is treated as economic compensation; common share count fell in 2025 but rose in H1 2026 alongside new common/preferred financing.
Owner Earnings remains UNKNOWN because maintenance versus growth AI infrastructure requirements cannot be bounded honestly.
unresolved_points: Maintenance AI capex is not disclosed.
Future dilution from mandatory conversion depends on stock price and capped-call settlement.

core_findings: Alphabet has a long record of funding high-return organic R&D and infrastructure, but the 2026 capital program is a step-change whose realized returns are unproven.

H1 2026 combined major uses included about $80.6bn capex, $33.7bn acquisition/intangible cash outflow and $22.1bn nonmarketable investment purchases; funding included common equity, mandatory preferred and debt.
Wiz ($29.5bn) and Intersect (~$5.9bn) materially increase acquisition capital; Wiz preliminary goodwill is about 77% of purchase consideration.
No H1 2026 repurchases occurred while new equity was issued; this is not automatically negative because funding needs rose, but per-share discipline must be judged on subsequent returns.
Other Bets continue to consume capital and lack consolidated standalone return disclosure.
unresolved_points: Wiz, Intersect and current AI infrastructure cohort returns are unproven.
Waymo cumulative return on invested capital remains unavailable.

core_findings: Operational execution is evidenced by sustained Search economics, Cloud scale/profitability and accelerated AI deployment, but management claims are not used as proof by themselves.
Seven of ten 2026 director nominees are independent; an independent chair and dedicated Risk and Compliance Committee strengthen formal oversight.
CEO compensation is more performance-weighted in 2026 and includes relative-TSR and Waymo/Wing value-creation conditions, plus minimum share-ownership requirements.
Founder super-voting control remains a material minority-governance asymmetry: Page and Brin together controlled a majority of voting power despite lower economic ownership.
unresolved_points: Founder control materially limits minority influence over board outcomes and strategic changes.
Compensation alignment does not prove capital-allocation returns.

core_findings: Reference class: dominant global digital platforms undergoing an interface transition and a large infrastructure investment cycle.
External evidence confirms unusually high Search/Chrome/Android usage shares, but also strong AI-model competition and large Meta/Amazon advertising scale.
Antitrust remedies treat distribution/defaults/data access as competitively material, preventing an assumption that observed share is purely organic preference.
No quantified base-rate dataset in the admitted evidence is strong enough to manufacture a numerical prior.
unresolved_points: No directly comparable historical platform transition provides a clean quantitative base rate for generative-AI Search economics.

core_findings: Liquidity is substantial, but headline net cash is an incomplete resilience measure because contractual/purchase obligations, uncommenced leases, infrastructure backstops and preferred claims are material.
Regulatory risk is structural across Search, adtech, Android/Play and UK/EU frameworks; remedies can affect distribution/data/interoperability independently of fines.
AI creates both disruption and execution risk: monetization, compute cost, model competition, copyright/security and publisher ecosystem effects remain live.

Infrastructure scaling is exposed to power/water/land constraints and a small set of specialized suppliers; operational incidents exist though the cited outage has no disclosed material consolidated loss.
Founder control is a governance concentration risk; advertising/Search remains a business concentration risk despite Cloud growth.
unresolved_points: Cash cost and behavioral effect of remedies remain uncertain.
The long-dated economic burden of $811bn contractual obligations depends on utilization, cancellation/conditionality and revenue generated by the infrastructure.

material_cross_block_reconciliations.issue: Strong Search moat versus antitrust/default dependence
material_cross_block_reconciliations.resolution: Moat existence is strongly supported, but trend is UNCLEAR and distribution-contract dependence is explicit negative evidence rather than ignored.

material_cross_block_reconciliations.issue: Strong Cloud segment margin versus AI capital intensity
material_cross_block_reconciliations.resolution: Cloud profitability is recognized, but shared AI R&D/capex allocation prevents treating segment margin as fully loaded ROIC proof.

material_cross_block_reconciliations.issue: Large runway versus weak H1 standardized FCF
material_cross_block_reconciliations.resolution: Growth opportunity and cash realization are separated; runway remains supported while cash score is lower and Owner Earnings remains UNKNOWN.
Cash/securities are retained as resilience, but $811bn obligations and off-balance-sheet commitments are separately stress-mapped and not netted away.
